AUDIT QUESTION: Batch 69 = RULING 73 (orchestrator 2026-11-13 '18:00'), verbatim: "THE CUT FOLLOWS THE LOCK'S WORDS. (a) OUT: the out point is never before the decoded END of the lock's LAST word. A pause inside the locked text is not a cut point, however long: the sentence law looks for the tail pause only AFTER the last locked word. (The hook ended on 'or' at a 130 ms pause before 'reissued'.) (b) IN: the in point is never more than 400 ms before the first locked word's onset (and never less than the head-lead rule requires: 80 ms, or the declared pad). Dead air before the first word is trimmed to that lead; if the audio in that lead is not quiet by the head rule, hold with that reason. (clip_01 opened 3.47 s before 'I'.) (c) Both are checked at the pin-stage pre-check service too (ruling 68 / 72), so the builder learns before the seal that a span cannot be cut to these rules. Must-fail tests: both of 13949b7c's spans fail on the old code and pass on the fix; the three delivered pins' cuts are unchanged by it (0c68b589, 41f29b1f, 37c5b5f5: same in / out to the frame, or say which moved and why)."
Background (measured on the real run pinned_20261113_221758):
- the hook's pause_out (26.99-27.12) lies inside the decoded last word 'reissued.' (26.66-27.54). boundary() searches the quiet run between the two words' MIDPOINTS (a guard for Whisper's off edges), and the hesitation run's end (27.12) just crosses the midpoint (27.10).
- clip_01's decode has a 4.58 s hole before 'I' (14.44). The IN pause found is a 60 ms dip at 10.96, so the clip opens on 3.47 s of non-speech (the second recogniser hears no words; Whisper hallucinates 'thank you').
The change (pipeline/sentence_law.py, pipeline/lock_precheck.py):
- boundary(..., tail=False): with tail=True (only the edge after a lock's last word) the pause is searched from words[k]['end'] to the next word's midpoint. A run inside the last word cannot be chosen; a run crossing the decoded end still can.
- edge_plan calls boundary(sa, words, i1, tail=True), then _ruling73(bin_, bout, words, i0, i1), which narrows the legal ranges:
  - OUT cut_lo >= words[i1]['end'];
  - IN cut_lo >= words[i0]['start'] - IN_LEAD_MAX_S (0.400). The cut is moved to start - LEAD_TARGET_S (0.25) when it was before the bound. A file head keeps its quiet up to the bound.
  - Not cuttable when the range empties, with a reason naming (ruling 73 a / b).
  - The head-lead rule is untouched: ruling 28's hook_lead (80 ms) and the D1 pad still run, now inside the narrowed range.
- accepted_cut: a cut placed at the boundary point (DEC-10 d valley / short gaps) is clamped into [cut_lo, cut_hi], so no path cuts outside the ranges. G16 (_edge_row) reads the same ranges.
- sentence_law.lock_cut(src, words, lock, label): write_lock_cut_table's per-segment body moved verbatim (edge_plan, accepted_cut, hook_lead for the hook, the trimmed onset rule). write_lock_cut_table calls it, and so does the pre-check (c): after ruling 17 / 72 a span whose lock stands is cut with it, and an error holds with "ruling 73: the render cannot cut this span: ...". RULES becomes "ruling 17 + ruling 72 + ruling 73".
MEASURED (the cut table recomputed with the old and the new code on the runs' own files):
- 13949b7c: hook OUT 27.09 -> 27.78 (after 'reissued.'s end); clip_01 IN 10.97 -> 14.04; clip_01 OUT +20 ms; clip_02 unchanged.
- 0c68b589: unchanged (its clip_01 OUT recomputes one 10 ms hop off with the OLD code too).
- Every OUT of every delivered pin: unchanged.
- ONE span moves IN: 'Bitcoin ... ever.' (41f29b1f's hook 14.38 -> 14.57; 37c5b5f5's clip_02 14.38 -> 14.69). It opened 0.56 s before its first word. It is also the protected medley reference's hook, so that reference's reproduction reports the changed decision (an orchestrator ruling is pending; not merged).
Tests:
- test_ruling73.py: _ruling73 unit tests (a, b, file head); the must-fail on 13949b7c's real run (fails on the old sentence_law, passes on the fix); the delivered pins' cuts unchanged but the named span (fails on the old code because the named span did not move).
- test_lock_precheck.py: a span the render cannot cut holds before the seal; a passing span records the render's cut.
- 32 passed.
FIND: a path that can still cut outside the narrowed ranges (OUT before the decoded end, IN more than 400 ms early); a behaviour change for spans the rule does not touch (the refactor of write_lock_cut_table must be verbatim); the head-lead rule weakened; a pre-check verdict that differs from the render's cut table for the same span; a test that does not test what it claims. +#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""RULING 73 (orchestrator 2026-11-13 '18:00'), THE CUT FOLLOWS THE LOCK'S WORDS. (a) OUT is never before the decoded
+end of the last locked word: the tail pause is searched only after it. (b) IN is never more than 400 ms before the first
+locked word's decoded start; dead air is trimmed. The head-lead rule is unchanged.
+MUST-FAIL on pin 13949b7c's real spans (run pinned_20261113_221758), held at prepare 17:23:
+- the hook's cut fell in 'or [130 ms] reissued.' inside the decoded last word (27.09 < 27.54);
+- clip_01 opened 3.47 s before 'I' (10.97 < 14.44 - 0.40).
+Both fail on the old sentence_law and pass on the fix. The delivered pins' cuts stay put, except ONE span measured and
+named (the medley reference's hook, 'Bitcoin ... ever.', which opened 0.56 s before its first word).
+Run: cd ~/protocol_pulse && CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= python3 -m pytest -q pipeline/test_ruling73.py"""
+import json
+import os
+import shutil
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+PIPELINE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+sys.path.insert(0, PIPELINE)
+import sentence_law as SL  # noqa: E402
+
+RUNS = "/home/ultron/protocol_pulse/runs"
+
+
+def words_at(*spans):
+    return [{"word": w, "start": a, "end": b} for w, a, b in spans]
+
+
+class TestTheRangesFollowTheLock(unittest.TestCase):
+    """_ruling73 on edge_plan's ranges (no audio)."""
+
+    def test_a_out_never_before_the_last_words_decoded_end(self):
+        w = words_at(("or", 26.30, 26.66), ("reissued.", 26.66, 27.54), ("Countries", 27.54, 28.08))
+        bout = {"valid": True, "cut_lo": 26.91, "cut_hi": 27.13, "cut": 27.09, "cuttable": True}
+        SL._ruling73({}, bout, w, 0, 1)
+        self.assertEqual((bout["cut_lo"], bout["cuttable"]), (27.54, False))
+        self.assertIn("(ruling 73 a)", bout["reason"])
+        ok = {"valid": True, "cut_lo": 31.35, "cut_hi": 31.6, "cut": 31.56, "cuttable": True}   # 41f29b1f clip_02
+        SL._ruling73({}, ok, words_at(("x", 31.0, 31.2), ("undervalued.", 31.2, 31.48)), 0, 1)
+        self.assertEqual((ok["cut_lo"], ok["cut"], ok["cuttable"]), (31.48, 31.56, True))
+
+    def test_b_in_never_more_than_400_ms_before_the_first_word(self):
+        w = words_at(("I", 14.44, 15.04), ("think,", 15.04, 15.52))
+        bin_ = {"valid": True, "cut_lo": 10.79, "cut_hi": 15.05, "cut": 10.96, "cuttable": True}
+        SL._ruling73(bin_, {}, w, 0, 1)
+        self.assertEqual((bin_["cut_lo"], bin_["cut"], bin_["cuttable"]), (14.04, 14.19, True))   # dead air trimmed
+        near = {"valid": True, "cut_lo": 14.16, "cut_hi": 14.3, "cut": 14.3, "cuttable": True}  # 37c5b5f5 clip_01
+        SL._ruling73(near, {}, words_at(("I", 14.36, 14.5)), 0, 0)
+        self.assertEqual((near["cut_lo"], near["cut"], "ruling73_in" in near), (14.16, 14.3, False))
+        none = {"valid": True, "cut_lo": 10.0, "cut_hi": 10.5, "cut": 10.2, "cuttable": True}     # no room at all
+        SL._ruling73(none, {}, words_at(("I", 14.44, 15.0)), 0, 0)
+        self.assertEqual((none["cut_lo"], none["cuttable"]), (14.04, False))
+        self.assertIn("(ruling 73 b)", none["reason"])
+
+    def test_b_a_file_head_keeps_its_quiet_up_to_the_bound(self):
+        head = {"valid": True, "file_head": True, "cut_lo": 0.0, "cut_hi": 13.0, "cut": 13.0, "cuttable": True}
+        SL._ruling73(head, {}, words_at(("Bitcoin", 14.0, 14.5)), 0, 0)

+def _recut(run):
+    """The run's cut table recomputed with THIS code on a scratch copy (sources / transcripts linked, edl copied)."""
+    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="r73t_")
+    try:
+        for sub in ("sources", "transcripts"):
+            os.symlink(os.path.join(run, sub), os.path.join(tmp, sub))
+        shutil.copy(os.path.join(run, "edl.json"), tmp)
+        return {c["clip_id"]: c for c in SL.write_lock_cut_table(tmp)}
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
+
+
+def _have(name):

+    return all(os.path.exists(os.path.join(r, x)) for x in ("edl.json", "sources", "transcripts", "cuts_final.json"))

+        self.assertTrue(self.cuts["hook"]["verified"], self.cuts["hook"].get("error"))
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(self.cuts["hook"]["cut_out"], end - 1e-9)          # old code: 27.09
+
+    def test_b_clip_01_opens_within_400_ms_of_i(self):
+        seg = self.edl["clips"][0]
+        start = self._words(seg["video_id"])[seg["selection_lock"]["i0"]]["start"]   # 'I' 14.44
+        self.assertTrue(self.cuts["clip_01"]["verified"], self.cuts["clip_01"].get("error"))
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(self.cuts["clip_01"]["cut_in"], round(start - SL.IN_LEAD_MAX_S, 3) - 1e-9)  # old: 10.97
+        self.assertLessEqual(self.cuts["clip_01"]["cut_in"], start)

+HOP = 0.0101
+MOVED = {("pinned_20261113_031328", "hook"): 14.57, ("pinned_20261112_165629", "clip_02"): 14.69}

+@unittest.skipUnless(all(_have(r) for r in ("pinned_20261113_211048", "pinned_20261113_031328",

+class TestTheDeliveredCuts(unittest.TestCase):
+    """0c68b589, 41f29b1f, 37c5b5f5: every cut as recorded (one 10 ms hop), except the one span that opened 0.56 s
+    before 'Bitcoin' (its IN moves to the ruling-73 bound: 41f29b1f's hook, 37c5b5f5's clip_02)."""
+
+    def test_unchanged_but_the_named_span(self):
+        for name in ("pinned_20261113_211048", "pinned_20261113_031328", "pinned_20261112_165629"):
+            run = os.path.join(RUNS, name)
+            old = {c["clip_id"]: c for c in json.load(open(os.path.join(run, "cuts_final.json")))}
+            new = _recut(run)
+            for cid, o in old.items():
+                n = new[cid]
+                self.assertLessEqual(abs(n["cut_out"] - o["cut_out"]), HOP, (name, cid, "out", o, n))
+                want_in = MOVED.get((name, cid), o["cut_in"])
+                self.assertLessEqual(abs(n["cut_in"] - want_in), HOP, (name, cid, "in", o, n))
+

+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
